items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I remember I was like a teenager. And you know Christian McBride’s maybe my age, maybe a year or so older. But he was kind of like a hot — I just remember looking at him and some other musicians and being like wow, those bass players are great.

ctx.x: So if you were a guest at one of the larger jazz schools, would you have advice? I want to say it was a gathering of bass players at Berklee, right? And you’ve been out in the business for years. Do you have anything you can tell them?

I mean I would say, well you know what I did too, I started bass a little late. Like I was a violin teacher, I mean a violin player. And I remember I was like a teenager. And you know Christian McBride’s maybe my age, maybe a year or so older. But he was kind of like a hot — I just remember looking at him and some other musicians and being like wow, those bass players are great. Like technically, I don’t know if I’m going to be that. So I thought to myself how can I distinguish myself you know. And so I figured…

Yeah, I have often thought that the bass is one of the harder instruments to show a personality. And there’s people that stick out in my mind, like Buster Williams, who God almighty, the sound he had. And I don’t know if it’s just ‘cause partly they knew how to record him or something, but.
